name: capell-app/widget-audio-playlist
description: Your recorded talks, sermons or episodes on a page as a playlist, with transcripts and chapters listeners can jump to.

marketplace.summary: An audio playlist of your uploaded files, with optional artwork, transcripts and chapter buttons that skip to the right moment.
marketplace.description: Put one to twenty uploaded recordings on a page as a playlist, in the order you set. Each track has a title and an artist, with artwork if you add it. Add a transcript and listeners can open it beneath the track. Name the parts of a recording with their start times and they appear as chapter buttons. Audio loads only once someone presses play. Tracks must be audio files uploaded to the Capell media library, so web links to outside players aren't accepted. It needs Layout Builder to place it on a page.
marketplace.problem: Recordings sit unheard, or live in someone else's player, with no written version and no way to skip ahead.
marketplace.outcome: Listeners pick a track from your list on your page, read the transcript and jump straight to the chapter they want.

faq.question: Can I use a Spotify or SoundCloud link?
faq.answer: No. The audio has to be files you upload to your own site, and any artwork has to be uploaded too.

faq.question: How many tracks can one playlist hold?
faq.answer: Between one and twenty. Listeners see them in the order you choose and play each one on the page.

faq.question: Can listeners read a transcript or jump to a chapter?
faq.answer: Yes, when you supply them. A written version opens under a Transcript heading, and each chapter becomes a button that jumps the track to its start time.

faq.question: Does the next track start by itself?
faq.answer: No. Each track plays when someone presses play, and starting another one pauses the first.
